design: Within one process and in the order that matters: fusion installs at node 424 BEFORE graph capture at 422, so the captured graphs contain the fused projections. Then restore both and re-capture unfused for the comparison.

result.verdict: neutral; if anything marginally worse, well inside noise

why_the_projection_failed: The 0.109 s projection came from isolated GEMM timings: three separate audio projections measured 0.1245 ms against 0.0412 ms fused, which is 193 GB/s against 583 GB/s. But those isolated calls each paid per-call dispatch overhead, and graph replay had ALREADY removed it. Inside a captured graph the three separate GEMMs run at roughly 3 x 15.5 us = 46 us, which is already close to the fused 41 us. Fusing removed overhead that was no longer there.
methodological_lesson: This is the same error as reading py-spy occupancy at a blocking call as removable latency: a cost measured in one execution context was assumed to exist in another. Any projection for the graph-replayed sampler must be measured under graph replay, not in isolation.
consequence: The 61.5%-of-roofline figure still stands, because it was derived by differencing real graph-replay timings at two token counts. But its CAUSE is not per-GEMM dispatch overhead, which graph replay already removes. Whatever keeps the blocks 1.82x above roofline is real GPU-side work, and fusing projections is not the lever for it.
status: Fusion is exact and retained as a correct-but-neutral mechanism. Not promoted.
